intended_object: The orthogonal direct sum ⊕_i A_i of a finite family of finite quadratic modules (finite abelian groups with a ℚ/ℤ-valued quadratic form). The underlying group is Π_i A_i, the form is q(x) = Σ_i q_i(x_i), and the bilinear pairing is the polar of q. This comes from the docstring and module doc (Nikulin §1.1).
explanation:
A `FiniteQuadraticModule` is a finite abelian group with a symmetric ℚ/ℤ-valued pairing and a quadratic map `QuadraticMap ℤ A (AddCircle 1)` whose polar form is that pairing.

The definition takes the carrier `∀ i, A i` and the quadratic map `QuadraticMap.pi`, which is Mathlib's x ↦ Σ_i q_i(x_i). The pairing is the polar bilinear form of that quadratic map, so the compatibility field holds by `rfl`. The lemma `pi_pairing` checks that this pairing equals the sum of the coordinate pairings, which is the usual orthogonal-sum pairing.

The carrier inherits its `AddCommGroup` and `Finite` instances from the Pi type. Finiteness needs ι to be finite, and the `[Fintype ι]` hypothesis supplies this; it also gives the finite sum in `QuadraticMap.pi`. So the restriction to finite families is exactly what the construction needs. It is not an artificial narrowing. Within finite families, any index type and any universe are allowed.

This is the standard orthogonal sum. Mathlib has the quadratic map `QuadraticMap.pi` that it builds on, but no bundled notion of a finite quadratic module, so nothing more general exists to compare against.
